cohort: 4358 women who delivered up to 12 months before the start of the study in rural areas of Maputo and Gaza provinces, Southern Mozambique
finding: The study found a high incidence of obstetric fistulae (1.1 per 1000 recently pregnant women) in an area with high numbers of facility births, highlighting delays in receiving appropriate care.
mod_finding: All but one woman with fistula had a Cesarean section, and all babies of these women died (four stillborn, one soon after birth).
